methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Apis Cor is a seed-stage construction technology company that has raised $5.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a private comparables universe of five companies operating in the housing and construction sector (BotBuilt, Unlimited Industries, Ground Control Development, ADMARES, and Hedral). No public market comps are available in this early-stage, specialized subsector.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($5.5M, approximated at $6M) as a valuation proxy and applying a standard seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $14M. This reflects typical dilution and value creation patterns between seed and Series A financings in venture-backed companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $12M to $16M, with $14M as the median point. This range incorporates a reasonable margin of error around the single-method estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of public benchmarks, limited data on private peer financials or revenue multiples, and the nascent stage of the addressable market in construction robotics. Refining this valuation would require additional data on comparable company revenue, unit economics, and progress toward measurable product-market validation milestones.
